📜 Revision Tracker — pre-month lock-in vs first forecast
Picks a forecast month and shows, per SKU: the first forecast Chewy gave you for that month, the final value locked in by the last snapshot taken before the month started, and the net revision between them. Past-month snapshots that arrived AFTER the month started don't count toward the lock — they're tracked separately as the latest current value.

🧮 How Amazon US fees + proceeds are calculated
Gross Sales — raw gross_sales from sku_economics. Pre-return revenue.
Net Sales — raw net_sales. After returns. For CA, this is in CAD natively; the "USD" toggle multiplies by 1 / pnlFxRate using the live rate from the Bank of Canada Valet API (with a 1.3681 fallback if the fetch fails).
Amazon Fees (the scorecard total) = sum of every fee line in the SKU Economics export:
  • fba_fulfillment_fee_total  ←  FBA Fulfillment (pick/pack/ship)
  • fba_storage_fee_total  ←  Monthly Storage
  • inbound_placement_fee_total  ←  Inbound Placement
  • inbound_transport_fee_total  ←  Inbound Transportation
  • low_inventory_fee_total  ←  Low Inventory Fee
  • aged_inventory_fee_total  ←  Aged Inventory Surcharge
  • removal_fee_total  ←  FBA Removal
  • storage_util_surcharge  ←  Storage Utilization Surcharge
  • referral_fee_total  ←  Referral Fee (Amazon's % of sale)
  • referral_fee_refunds_total  ←  Referral fee refunds (credits on returned orders)
  • refund_admin_fee_total  ←  Refund Administration Fee
Ad Spend (sponsored_products_total) is reported as its own scorecard, NOT included in the Amazon Fees total above.
Net Proceeds = net_proceeds_total as Amazon reports it (= Gross Sales − Refunds − Amazon Fees − Ad Spend + FBA Reimbursements + any misc adjustments). Use this as the authoritative bottom-line — the dashboard does not recompute it.
Total COGS = amazon_cogs × net_units_sold (from product_cogs.amazon_cogs, edited on the COGS page). Products with sales but no Amazon COGS are flagged in the missing-COGS banner above the scorecards.
Contribution Profit = Net Proceeds − Total COGS.
Margin % = Net Proceeds / Net Sales. After all Amazon fees + ad spend, before COGS.
Contribution % = Contribution Profit / Net Sales. After everything including COGS.
Period-over-period delta on each scorecard compares to the equal-length window immediately before the current range, restricted to the same set of products (selection if any, else the post-quick-filter visible set). Cost metrics (Fees / Ad Spend / COGS) color the delta inverted — a fee increase reads red.
🧮 How EU fees + proceeds are calculated
Net Sales — raw net_sales from sku_economics_eu. Native currency (GBP for GB rows, EUR for others) × the FX multiplier when "USD" mode is selected.
Amazon Fees (consolidated) =
  • Fulfilment by Amazon fulfilment fees total  ←  "FBA Fulfilment" in the breakdown. This column already includes Base fulfilment + Fuel/logistics surcharge as sub-components, so we don't add those separately.
  • + Digital Services Fee (FBA Fulfilment fees) total  ←  "Digital Services Fee — FBA Fulfilment". EU-specific surcharge, kept in its own field (NOT collapsed into a US/CA bucket).
  • + Digital Services Fee (Selling on Amazon fees) total  ←  "Digital Services Fee — Selling". Same — EU-specific, distinct field.
  • + Referral fee total  ←  "Referral Fee".
  • + Sponsored Products charge total  ←  reported separately as the Ad Spend scorecard, not lumped into Amazon Fees.
Net Proceeds = net_proceeds_total as Amazon reports it (= Net Sales − Amazon Fees). Sanity-checked against the row breakdown.
Total COGS = amazon_cogs_eu × net_units_sold (falls back to amazon_cogs when the EU column is blank). Edit per-product on the COGS page.
Contribution Profit = Net Proceeds − Total COGS.
Not in this column set: Base fulfilment per-unit, Fuel surcharge per-unit (both rolled into FBA Fulfillment). These are accessible via the raw sku_economics_eu table if you need to decompose further — open Data → Query Database.

🎯 Top Action Items — invest / cut recommendations
Composite score across conversion, sessions, ad spend, ad headroom, contribution % and revenue. INVEST = profitable products with room to spend more · CUT = ad spend leaking against contribution. Click 📌 Flag on any row to save to Change Log.
▾ collapse
🧪 Scenario modeling — what-if ad spend adjustments
Model shifts across the invest / cut lists. Real ROAS = Amazon-attributed sales ÷ ad spend (v8.13 — was TROAS). Marginal = real × 0.7 (moderate diminishing returns). Cuts assume same marginal — the LEAST productive $ is removed first.
▸ expand
🎯 Sessions × Conversion — quadrant scatter
X = Sessions (log scale). Y = Conversion %. Bubble size = Net Sales. Dashed lines are the median split. Top-Left = 🎯 STARVED · Top-Right = 🌟 STARS · Bottom-Left = 🌱 NICHE · Bottom-Right = 💸 BLEEDING. Click any bubble to focus the tables on that product. Uncheck rows in the tables to hide them from the chart.
🎯 Session-starved high converters — spend more
Products converting above median but pulling below-median sessions. Every extra visitor is likely to convert at the shown rate — increasing ad budget here is the highest-ROI move. Sorted by conversion desc.
💸 High-traffic low-converters — fix PDP before more ad spend
Products pulling above-median sessions but converting below median, with meaningful ad spend. Every ad dollar buys traffic that doesn't buy. Fix the PDP (images / bullets / A+ / price / reviews) before turning up the budget. Sorted by ad spend desc — worst money-losers first.
🌟 Stars — above-median sessions AND above-median conversion
The winners — high traffic + high conversion. Already efficient; protect them (defend rank, watch reviews / Buy Box, keep inventory in stock). Sorted by net sales desc — the biggest revenue drivers first.
🌱 Niche — below-median sessions AND below-median conversion
Small products with weak conversion. Not an obvious spend target — investigate whether the listing works at all before deciding to invest, discontinue, or leave in maintenance mode. Sorted by conversion desc so any bright spots surface first.
Per-ASIN breakdown of every sku_economics row matching the current filters (region/period/brand/category/search). Built to find Looker-vs-app discrepancies — unmatched ASINs hiding fees, suspect duplicates, off-Monday weeks, brand misattributions.
⚠ Unmatched ASINs
ASINs present in sku_economics but missing from products. They carry fees / ad spend that the Brand filter currently drops. Add them to the products catalog (or pick a brand to assign them to) so their costs roll up correctly.
📋 Matched ASINs (per-row)
Every ASIN being summed into the P&L Summary view, including the product brand we matched it to. Useful for spotting brand misattributions (an ASIN here under "Doggijuana" that Looker counts as something else, or vice versa).
📅 Week-start hygiene
Amazon SKU Economics rows where week_start isn't a Monday. Past versions (v4.91, v4.92) had timezone-poisoned parsers that produced shifted dates — leftover rows from those uploads would show up here. Should be empty in current data.
⚠ Possible duplicate weeks
ASINs that have ≥2 sku_economics rows for the same calendar week under different week_start values (typically off-by-a-day or off-by-a-week from a re-upload). Each such pair inflates the totals because both rows are summed.

🧮 Pricing Scenarios
Model a bulk-pack price against a reference single-pack, with a cannibalization-risk gauge based on per-base-pack discount.
Reference product (the single-pack you're protecting)
Bulk Scenarios
How cannibalization risk is scored
Discount % = (single_MSRP − bulk_price_per_base_pack) ÷ single_MSRP
• 🟢 LOW (0–14% off) — bulk buyers self-select (subscribers, gifters, heavy users); single-pack stays the impulse buy.
• 🟡 MODERATE (15–24% off) — starts pulling some single-pack customers to bulk; net-positive if incremental sales lift > 2× the cannibalized margin.
• 🔴 HIGH (25%+ off) — most habitual single-pack buyers will upgrade; risks a permanent margin reset on your best SKU.
COGS estimate — bulk COGS = base COGS × pack size (scales linearly). No packaging economies-of-scale modeled — set the "Custom bulk COGS" field if you have a firm quote for the multi-pack tray/box.
